research_question: Why do heavy steel ships float instead of sinking?

sources.title: Build a Boat
notes: Buoyancy equals the weight of displaced fluid; hull volume allows a ship to displace enough water to balance its weight.

sources.title: Boat Building Challenge
notes: Archimedes' principle explains buoyancy; hull shape and displaced volume matter more than whether the material itself is denser than water.

sources.title: Archimedes' Principle
notes: A submerged body experiences an upward force equal to the weight of displaced fluid; equilibrium requires buoyancy to balance weight.
